pageCache.text:
An International School in London
30
5-Years Average Diploma Score
50+
Student/teacher ratio
11th
Small Independent School
An IB education goes beyond academic achievement. At ICS London, students develop curiosity, critical thinking and a global perspective while learning in a diverse international community.
Our approach combines academic excellence with inclusion, wellbeing and personal development. Students are encouraged to become open-minded, caring and confident members of an international community.
For children aged 3 to 5, our Early Years Programme creates a supportive environment where learning happens through play, exploration and discovery.
Children develop confidence, independence and essential social skills while building the foundations for their future education.
For students aged 5 to 11, the Primary Years Programme encourages children to ask questions, explore ideas and make connections between their learning and the world around them.
Through inquiry-based learning, students develop both academic knowledge and the skills needed to become confident, independent learners.
Our secondary curriculum provides students with a balanced academic journey through the IB Middle Years Programme and IGCSE.
Our Core Values in International Education
Developing Independent Thinkers Through the Middle Years Programme
The MYP encourages students to think critically, make connections between subjects and apply their learning to real-world situations.
Building a Strong Foundation Through IGCSE
From ages 14 to 16, students can follow IGCSE courses that provide strong academic foundations while preparing them for the IB Diploma Programme.
The IB Diploma Programme
For students aged 16 to 18, the IB Diploma Programme combines academic depth with independent research, critical thinking and global perspectives.
Why Choose the IB at ICS London?
The IB Diploma encourages students to take ownership of their learning while developing the skills and confidence needed for university and future careers.
AN INTERNATIONAL COMMUNITY
We offer a warm welcome to international students from over 50 nationalities. ICS London is one of only two Central London schools to offer the full IB (ages 3-18). We also offer IGCSEs to students aged 14 to 16.
NURTURING UNIQUE JOURNEYS We offer a truly personalised learning experience, tailoring our curriculum to the student's interests.
THE WORLD FROM OUR CLASSROOM Study the IB at ICS London, one of the UK’s most experienced IB World Schools.
BEYOND THE CLASSROOM Discover how we deliver enriching experiences beyond the classroom.
EARLY YEARS
This programme is for young children aged 3-5 years old who love to learn, play and explore.
PRIMARY SCHOOL
For children aged 5-11. An inquiry-led learning framework which develops skills in real-life contexts.
MIDDLE SCHOOL
For students aged 11 to 16, two balanced programmes to prepare them for the IB Diploma Programme.
DIPLOMA PROGRAMME
This pre-university programme is for students aged 16-18.
PRIMARY CAMPUS
Housed in a renovated Victorian building in Marylebone Westminster, Central London.
SECONDARY CAMPUS
Located within minutes from our Primary Campus, in the heart of Central London.
Last week, a group of our Year 11 and 12 students enjoyed an inspiring day trip to Paris, where they had the unique opportunity to visit the UNESCO Headquarters.
ICS London is celebrating another outstanding achievement following success at this year’s Globeducate Debate, the annual international debating event that brings together Globeducate schools from around the world in a dynamic online competition.
We are proud to celebrate our Secondary PE and Maths Teacher, Mr. Jared, who successfully completed the London Marathon yesterday with an outstanding official time of 3:09:26.
The Summer Term at ICS London began on a high note with our vibrant Whole School Charity Fun Run, held at Paddington Recreation Ground. It was an afternoon filled with energy, enthusiasm, and a strong sense of community spirit.
It has been an incredibly exciting and inspiring week for both primary and secondary students at ICS London, as the school came together to celebrate Eco Week through a diverse range of creative and educational activities.
Two of our Year 12 students recently travelled to France to take part in the annual Globeducate Model United Nations (MUN), accompanied by Ms Ilaria. The event provided an enriching opportunity for students to collaborate with peers from around the world while exploring some of today’s most pressing global issues.
This week Diploma Program students (with a few Year 11s) visited the The Guardian publishing house in King’s Cross. Experts in the field guided ICS London students through an investigation into how young people consume news today and what makes a news app relevant and engaging.
We are delighted to share that a group of our students recently took part in the Globeducate Academic Olympics, an inspiring annual event that brings together talented young thinkers from across the Globeducate network. This year’s competition was hosted by our sister schools ICS Milan and BES, who provided an exceptional environment for collaboration, creativity, and innovation.
As part of the Globeducate Agenda Events, students in Years 7–9 took part this week in the WWF Wild Wisdom Global Challenge. Although the challenge is primarily aimed at Secondary students, it is open to all learners aged 10-14, giving a wide range of young people the chance to explore global biodiversity and environmental issues in an engaging, interactive way
On Friday, our pupils from Early Years to Year 6 took part in Outdoor Classroom Day, a wonderful celebration of learning beyond the classroom walls.

pageCache.pageTitle: ICS' History & Mission - International School London, UK
pageCache.text:
History and Mission
The mission and vision underpin our guiding principles to ensure students grow and develop to realise future success in higher education and their chosen careers.
ICS London Mission
“Our innovative approach to education inspires each and every student to discover their strengths within a community of future leaders."
ICS London Vision
“We aim to be a community of compassionate and inspired world citizens."
The International Community School (ICS), as it was known, opened its doors in Marylebone, central London, in 1979.
The school has grown and developed over the years and is now one of just a small group of IB World Schools offering the full International Baccalaureate (IB) programme. The school was formed upon a set of principles that the founders believed should underpin any school designed for the modern age. These included values such as freedom, internationalism, democracy, respect and the rule of law, and these are still part of the ICS London philosophy today.
We are kind, compassionate and respectful. We take care of ourselves, our global community, and our environment.
We always do the right thing, even when it's challenging. We are honest, open minded, reliable and fair.
We are all lifelong learners, committed to becoming our best selves. We embrace failure and mistakes as opportunities to reflect and learn.
We are creative leaders who inspire each other to be innovative and discover our full potential.
The International Community School (ICS) was founded in 1979 by the Toettcher family. It was initially an English-language school for the children of diplomats and global business people based in London, but it quickly grew into a fully-fledged academic school based on the English national curriculum.
The International Community School (ICS) introduced the International Baccalaureate as a more relevant curriculum for students coming from different parts of the world. The school then extended the IB offering to include the Diploma Programme (Years 12-13) as well as the Primary Years Programme (Nursery-Year 6), and Middle Years Programme (Years 7-11).
In 2017, The International Community School (ICS) became integrated into the global NACE Schools group. Based in Spain, the NACE Schools Group had more than 50 schools worldwide.
NACE Schools group becomes Globeducate, a network of 60+ premium international schools and online programmes educating more than 40,000 students in over 12 different countries and on four continents. Being one of the four largest international school groups in the world provides internationally mobile parents and students with a choice of leading schools across Europe and the Middle East.
The International Community School (ICS) becomes ICS London with the ICS brand growing across Europe with schools in Paris, Milan, Rome and Nice. With the recognition that ICS London was the leading IB school in the Globeducate Group, the growth of the ICS schools in Europe is testament to the quality of teaching and student academic achievement.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to our IB School - International School London, UK
pageCache.text:
Head's Welcome
A Message From the Head of School
Serving and leading our diverse international community is an absolute privilege. As the Head of School, I extend a sincere and warm welcome to families contemplating joining us on our exceptional educational journey.
The decision to choose the right school for your child is a significant and at times, a challenging one. We genuinely understand the importance of this choice in shaping your child's educational path. Our mission is to take an innovative approach to education, inspiring each student to discover their strengths within a community of future leaders.
We are dedicated to living and breathing this mission, striving for excellence in every aspect of our school. Our ultimate goal is to see our students develop holistically, motivated to be the best version of themselves each day. With the exceptional support we provide, we empower students to unlock their potential.
Our vision extends to creating a community of compassionate and inspired global citizens. Embracing inclusivity, we acknowledge the uniqueness of every child and maintain a delicate balance between academic and pastoral support. Our staff ensures that each student is treated as an individual, fostering a personalised and innovative approach to learning.
We take immense pride in the achievements of all our students, working tirelessly to ensure each student feels valued in our school community. Regular celebrations throughout the school are aligned with our vision and mission.
Our commitment to small class sizes and a tailored learning approach has yielded remarkable results, including a 100% acceptance rate into first-choice universities. ICS London consistently ranks among the top 10 IB small schools in the country. Embracing students from diverse backgrounds—representing over 50 nationalities—our commitment to diversity fosters an environment where students from various cultural backgrounds learn and develop together. We actively promote kindness, compassion, and respect, caring for ourselves, our global community, and our environment.
At ICS London, we are all lifelong learners, committed to becoming our best selves. Our teachers create a nurturing classroom environment while providing an appropriate level of challenge. We encourage students to embrace failure and mistakes as opportunities to reflect and learn. Every member of our community is urged to be innovative and realise their true capabilities. We teach resilience by consistently striving to do the right thing, even when faced with challenges. Upholding values such as honesty, open-mindedness, reliability, and fairness, we prepare every child to make a positive impact in an ever-changing and increasingly challenging world.
ICS London transcends being just a school; it is a second home. As you step through our doors, you will sense the incredible support and a place where students feel a profound sense of belonging. I strongly encourage you to visit us and experience it firsthand. We look forward to welcoming you to ICS London.

pageCache.pageTitle: Secondary PE & Maths Teacher Completes the London Marathon in Impressive Time | News Details
pageCache.text:
Secondary PE & Maths Teacher Completes the London Marathon in Impressive Time
We are proud to celebrate our Secondary PE and Maths Teacher, Mr. Jared, who successfully completed the London Marathon yesterday with an outstanding official time of 3:09:26.
Running as part of World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF), Mr. Jared described the day as a fantastic experience. He shared how the incredible atmosphere and encouragement from the crowds helped carry him through the race, making all the hours of training truly worthwhile.
The event was made even more special by the presence of teachers and students who came out to support him along the route. Their cheers, alongside the energy of the wider crowd, played a huge role in keeping spirits high throughout the marathon.
Jared is also nearing an important milestone in his fundraising efforts. He has raised £2,325, reaching 93% of his £2,500 target, and is now just £175 away from his goal.
Reflecting on the experience, Mr. Jared said he is “absolutely thrilled” to have achieved his target time and expressed heartfelt thanks to everyone who has supported him—whether through donations or by cheering him on during the race.
We congratulate Mr. Jared on this remarkable achievement and wish him the very best as he pushes toward his fundraising goal.

Early Years (ages 3-5)
Discover Learning Through Play & Outdoor Learning for Early Years
We aim to create a sense of community and instil a passion for learning in every student, including our very youngest learners.
ICS London is an independent school which offers a fee-paying Early Years Programme as a part of our IB Primary Years curriculum. Our Early Years programme is a part of the Primary Years Programme (PYP). The PYP (ages 3-11) is the first of the three stages of the International Baccalaureate (IB) Programme that form a continuum of international education. The first stage focuses on nurturing and developing young children, moulding them into caring, active participants in a lifelong learning journey.
Outdoor Learning
Outdoor Learning plays an essential role in Early Years education. At ICS London, we offer all children regular outdoor learning opportunities to develop their personal, social and emotional skills, enhance creativity and bring our curriculum to life.
Our outdoor learning sessions are planned by our dedicated teachers alongside our Forest School Leader. They are led by the interest of learners. Children enjoy experiences from across the curriculum including telling stories, hunting for invertebrates, making mud pies and exploring habitats.
Outdoor learning builds on the natural instinct to learn that everyone is born with and offers opportunities to make choices, initiate learning and take risks which supports the development of positive attitudes and behaviour.
Read more about our Outdoor Learning Programme
Nurturing Environment Dedicated experienced teachers
Early Years Programme Exceptional early childhood development
Forest School Programme Develop personal, social and emotional skills
“The teachers are fantastic human beings first, then fantastic teachers.”
Learning Through Play
Play-based learning is an approach to learning that is child-led and open-ended play. It helps children develop social skills, motivation to learn, and language & numeracy skills.
At ICS London, we believe in providing opportunities for children to play and explore whilst learning about the world around them. The classroom environment is carefully planned by our specialist Early Years teachers to promote independent, confident and successful learners, which results in a lifelong love of learning and success.
Perfect Preparation for the PYP
Early years students at ICS London receive a fun introduction to the world of education, and are able to continue their journey through the Primary Years Programme (PYP) once they pass the age of 5 years old.

pageCache.pageTitle: Language Provision - International Community School London
pageCache.text:
Language Provision
Language Bridges: Connecting Cultures at ICS London
Discover the Power of Language at ICS London! Explore our language provision, offering courses in French, Spanish, and Mandarin alongside English proficiency training. Immerse yourself in diverse cultures and broaden your horizons through transformative language learning experiences
At ICS London, we aspire to nurture a genuine passion for languages among our students and foster an appreciation for diverse cultures, empowering them to thrive in our interconnected world. Our approach to language education is rigorous, offering cognitive benefits and deeper insights into English while nurturing fluency in the language of their choice. We take pride in our track record of inspiring students to continue their language learning journey, with 100% of our pupils studying at least one additional language at both IGCSE and DP levels.
In the Early Years Programme (EYFS), our Nursery & Reception classes, students as young as age 3 have the opportunity to begin learning a language.
Depending upon their current level of English, the children have the chance to learn French, Spanish, or Mandarin Chinese through our play-based approach. This language provision continues through our Primary Years Programme (PYP) as the students continue to receive two hours of language instruction twice a week.
In the Middle Years Programme (MYP) spanning Years 7-9, students embark on a bespoke language course also in French, Spanish, or Mandarin Chinese. Our language instructors are native speakers, ensuring authenticity and excellence in teaching. With our small class sizes, we tailor the curriculum to cater to each student's individual proficiency level. At the IGCSE level, all students are required to continue studying at least one of these three languages. Moreover, students proficient in an additional language or mother tongue may opt for an early IGCSE examination upon enrollment.
Continuous assessment occurs through regular vocabulary tests, homework assignments, and classroom engagements. Formal, external assessments take place at the conclusion of Year 11 (IGCSE) and Year 13 (DP), where students sit examinations administered by recognized exam boards.
We enthusiastically welcome students who speak additional languages alongside English at home or are independently learning languages. If you desire your child to pursue a qualification in a non-curricular language, please reach out to our admissions department for personalized guidance.
Pupils learning each modern language may have the opportunity to meet and converse with native speaking teachers as well as other pupils for whom French, Spanish, or Mandarin Chinese is a first language as we are a truly international school with students from all over the globe. Our school also offers a variety of language clubs and societies across both the Primary and Secondary schools which have previously included such extra curriculars as Latin club, Arabic club, and Chinese Culture club, etc.
“Education is extremely important to us and I can see that my child is really learning at ICS London, not only getting knowledge but also learning how to find it, encouraged to be curious, look for solutions, be creative, be proud of herself and others.”
-Anna, Year 3 Parent

pageCache.pageTitle: Year 11 and 12 Students Visit UNESCO Headquarters in Paris | News Details
pageCache.text:
Year 11 and 12 Students Visit UNESCO Headquarters in Paris
Last week, a group of our Year 11 and 12 students enjoyed an inspiring day trip to Paris, where they had the unique opportunity to visit the UNESCO Headquarters.
The visit provided students with a fascinating insight into the work of UNESCO and its mission to promote international cooperation through education, science, culture and communication. As they explored the iconic headquarters, students learned about the organisation's history, its global impact, and the role it plays in fostering peace and understanding between nations.
A highlight of the day was the chance to visit areas of the building that are not usually accessible to visitors, including the General Conference Room, where representatives from member states meet to discuss important global issues.
Reflecting on the experience, Eva said:
"Thank you so much for guiding us through the UNESCO headquarters last week. It was very interesting to learn about the history, formation and mission of UNESCO. I especially found it intriguing to learn about the artworks. The overall highlight of this trip was visiting the conference room. It was inspiring to be in a room where such important global decisions are made. Thank you again for sharing the importance of UNESCO with us."
Ruby also enjoyed discovering how art and architecture are woven into the identity of the organisation:
"I really enjoyed learning about the UNESCO building and feel like I gained a good understanding of what the organisation is about. It was interesting to see how much art was incorporated into the architecture and landscaping, all with so much intention and meaning. I also appreciated the opportunity to visit conference rooms that visitors do not usually get to see. The tour inspired me to learn more about UNESCO."
Shiomi reflected on how the visit broadened her understanding of the organisation's work:
"I would like to thank UNESCO, especially the officer who led our guided tour, and Ms Ann Beatty for facilitating this visit. Before the trip, I thought UNESCO mainly focused on world peace and art. The tour showed me the rich history of the organisation and how much it does for schools and science around the world. Our guide made complex global ideas easy to understand, and seeing the General Conference Room was fascinating. Walking through the headquarters really showed me how hard people work to bring different countries together."
The trip was a memorable and enriching experience, allowing students to connect their classroom learning with real-world global issues. We are grateful to UNESCO for hosting our students and providing such an engaging and educational visit.

pageCache.pageTitle: From IB to University - International School London, UK
pageCache.text:
University & Careers
Each stage taught at ICS London – from the Primary Years Programme (Nursery to Year 6), Middle Years Programme (Years 7 to 9), iGCSE Programme (Years 10 & 11) and International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme (Years 12 & 13) – forms just one part of a student's greater educational journey.
It's a journey which continues after students leave ICS London for university or the working world, and one which we believe never stops. It's our goal to share these beliefs with our students, so the positive foundations we help to build from early life serve our graduates for the rest of their lives.
Ranked in the top 20% of UK schools, ICS London is proud to claim an average IBDP student score of 30.8 points over the last 5 years – significantly higher than the pass point of 24 points, as well as the entry requirement of 26 points used by many universities.
A recognised qualification
As a qualification, the IBDP is accepted as a passport to entry by over 5,000 academic institutions around the world, including universities in the United Kingdom, the United States of America and over 100 other countries.
We produce informed, compassionate global citizens to help shape a better world. Recent graduates have gone on to some of the greatest universities in the world, from the US and Canada to Spain, Hong Kong, Australia and many other nations.
40% of our University Destinations are ranked among the Top 100 Universities in the World (according to The Times Higher Education University Ranking 2021).
Continued Development of Inquisitive Minds
Not only do our students go on to study at their university of choice, they also pursue study paths that match their skillset but also their passions and interests including:
Whatever a student's passion, talent, or area of interest, we ensure they receive all the encouragement and tutelage they need to perform at their very best, and to be ready to continue their academic journey in the world of higher education.
"The academic rigour that ICS London helped ignite within me has helped me achieve promising results for my first year at university. Ultimately, I would not be the person I am today without the experiences I had at ICS London. "

About to Start?
Whether you are a student about to start at ICS London, or the parent/guardian of a new starter, there are a few things to arrange and get familiar with ahead of the first day at school.
Be Informed
ICS London is dedicated to providing the best educational opportunities for all students, and the involvement of parents and guardians is key to delivering on that promise.
We recommend that all new students and their parents/guardians get to know our policies around areas such as:
This information and more can be found in the school's parent handbooks.
expectations (of students, staff and parents)
behaviour
punctuality and attendance
homework
online safety
plagiarism
Toddle
Students' educational progress is tracked using the Toddle system, which allows parents, teachers and students access to homework assignments, student reports and more.
Login information is provided to all students and parents/guardians upon starting at ICS London.
At ICS London we provide all secondary students with Microsoft Surface Pro devices that they can use in school and outside of school to support their studies. Primary students have access to iPads and laptops under adult supervision, facilitated by our stringent safeguarding system that restricts access to inappropriate content, fostering a technology-rich, guided learning environment for every student's success.
All IBDP students are expected to bring an advanced calculator.
School Uniform
Students in both our Primary and Secondary School are required to wear a school uniform, which consists of compulsory and optional items.
All students must wear appropriate attire for physical education lessons and bring a suitable swimming costume and towel for swimming lessons (goggles and swim caps are optional).
For primary students we recommend labelling all student clothing, as it makes it much easier to return lost items to their owners.
Find out more about our uniform here
Useful Information for the School
Prior to starting at ICS London, please let us know any specific information that will help us provide the educational experience you expect. This might include:
If you're unsure of anything or have any questions about preparing to start at ICS London, please feel free to contact the school directly.
Interested in our Transport Service?
Parents and guardians are welcome to bring students to, and collect them from, school each day. An optional bus service operates within certain zones, offering door-to-door transport solutions for students of all ages.

Parents' Guide
ICS London provides the ideal education for any student, and in particular those in London's international community.
Reasons for this include our location – close to all central London landmarks, while situated in the diplomatic quarter – our friendly and well-appointed campuses and our world-class teaching faculty.
But beyond that, we believe ICS London gives students the best start in life thanks to two fundamental areas where we will never compromise on quality: academics and student welfare.
The International Baccalaureate (IB) has been described as the gold standard in international education, with IB students found to enjoy greater success than their peers in areas such as attaining a first choice university, and possessing a globally-informed perspective.
At ICS London we press this advantage even further, with our graduates attaining an average student IB score of 30.8 – far higher than the pass point of 24.
With a completed IB Diploma from ICS London, graduates are ready and qualified to join the world's most prestigious universities, including those in the UK, the USA and in over 100 other countries around the globe.
To find out more about the International Baccalaureate, click here.
Safety is always our number one priority, and we work hard to ensure all students at ICS London may learn from a place of emotional, mental and physical security.
Many other top schools may offer similar promises, but where we differ is in our commitment to developing and maintaining a truly global context for all learning, in an environment where all voices are heard.
We're committed to inspiring the next generation of leaders, but just as committed to making them compassionate, understanding and informed citizens of the global community.
See the wellbeing page for further information.

pageCache.pageTitle: A Fantastic Start to the Summer Term: Whole School Charity Fun Run | News Details
pageCache.text:
A Fantastic Start to the Summer Term: Whole School Charity Fun Run
The Summer Term at ICS London began on a high note with our vibrant Whole School Charity Fun Run, held at Paddington Recreation Ground. It was an afternoon filled with energy, enthusiasm, and a strong sense of community spirit.
From our youngest learners in Nursery to our Year 10 students, everyone took part with determination and joy. While older students completed laps around the track, our youngest runners gave it their all on the hockey pitch. Joined by many supportive parents, the event was a true celebration of teamwork and perseverance, with participants aiming to complete as many laps as possible for a meaningful cause.
This year, we are proud to be raising funds for World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF), an international organisation dedicated to protecting wildlife, preserving natural habitats, and addressing the urgent challenges of climate change. We selected WWF as our chosen charity as it is one of the valued partners of Globeducate, reflecting our shared commitment to sustainability and global responsibility. Every step taken by our students contributed to this important mission.
Throughout the afternoon, our school values were on full display. Students demonstrated respect, resilience, integrity, and courage in every lap they ran, encouraging one another and pushing themselves to achieve their best.
We extend our sincere thanks to the Secondary Student Council for their leadership in organising such a successful event, to our staff for their dedication and support, and to our parent community for their encouragement and enthusiasm. Most importantly, congratulations to all our students—every lap truly made a difference.
We would also like to wish the best of luck to our Secondary School PE Teacher, Mr. Jared, who will be taking on the London Marathon this Sunday in support of WWF. We are incredibly proud of his commitment and wish him every success!

ICS LONDON Curriculum
ICS London delivers a bespoke curriculum that is rooted in the International Baccalaureate (IB) framework, which culminates in the IB Diploma. Catering for students aged 3 to 18, ICS London offers a truly personalised education to all our young learners, balancing challenge, support and fun.
Universities in the UK, USA and more than 100 other countries accept the IB, many requiring a pass mark of 24 or 26 – comfortably below ICS London's average student score of 30.8.
From a child's first steps into the world of education, all the way through to higher education, ICS London delivers a best-in-class learning experience, with results to match.
The IB Learner Profile and Approaches to Learning (ATL) are deliberately explored across the school to develop those desirable skills of critical thinking, self-management, communication, research and interpersonal working.
All students receive a personal development class each week as well as tutor time each morning.
On the secondary site the curriculum is broken into three: MYP, iGCSE and IBDP. To explore what is taught at each of these stages in a little more detail, please follow the links below.

We thoughtfully consider the world and our own ideas and experience. We work to understand our strengths and weaknesses in order to support our learning and personal development.
We critically appreciate our own cultures and personal histories, as well as the values and traditions of others. We seek and evaluate a range of points of view, and we are willing to grow from the experience.
We nurture our curiosity, developing skills for inquiry and research. We know how to learn independently and with others. We learn with enthusiasm and sustain our love of learning throughout life.
We show empathy, compassion and respect. We have a commitment to service, and we act to make a positive difference in the lives of others and in the world around us.
We express ourselves confidently and creatively in more than one language and in many ways. We collaborate effectively, listening carefully to the perspectives of other individuals and groups.
We understand the importance of balancing different aspects of our lives—intellectual, physical, and emotional—to achieve well-being for ourselves and others. We recognize our interdependence with other people and with the world in which we live.
We develop and use conceptual understanding, exploring knowledge across a range of disciplines. We engage with issues and ideas that have local and global significance.
We approach uncertainty with forethought and determination; we work independently and cooperatively to explore new ideas and innovative strategies. We are resourceful and resilient in the face of challenges and change.
We act with integrity and honesty, with a strong sense of fairness and justice, and with respect for the dignity and rights of people everywhere. We take responsibility for our actions and their consequences.
We use critical and creative thinking skills to analyse and take responsible action on complex problems. We exercise initiative in making reasoned, ethical decisions.
We are an inclusive school and welcome students from across the world. As a small, boutique school, we are able to personalise our curriculum provision to meet the needs and interests of most students. There is a one to one and/or small group provision for EAL and a variety of learning differences where required. Our bespoke provision means that students can work towards qualifications beyond their age to fit with international programmes and interests.

IB Diploma Programme (DP)
At ICS London, we are an accredited IB World School with extensive experience of delivering the International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme (IBDP). The Diploma is an internationally recognised qualification, respected by universities in the UK and around the world, and provides students with a strong academic foundation for their next steps in higher education and beyond.
Our IB Diploma students, aged 16 to 18, are supported by experienced and dedicated teachers who understand the importance of balancing academic challenge with personal development. Students are encouraged to think independently, explore their interests and develop the confidence to take responsibility for their learning. Through a personalised approach, we help each student build the knowledge, skills and resilience needed to thrive in a rapidly changing world.
Why Choose the IB Diploma Programme at ICS London?
The two-year IB Diploma Programme offers students a broad and balanced education that encourages them to explore different subjects while developing a deeper understanding of their chosen areas of study. At ICS London, students benefit from a supportive learning environment where teachers know them as individuals and can help them make informed choices about their academic pathway.
The programme also develops skills that extend beyond subject knowledge, including critical thinking, communication, research, organisation and independent learning. These skills can support students as they transition from school to university and prepare for future academic and professional opportunities.
A Broad and Balanced Curriculum
Students study a range of subjects across the IB Diploma curriculum, allowing them to develop both breadth and depth in their learning. Subject choices include Language and Literature, Mathematics, Sciences, Humanities, Languages, Business and Visual Arts.
The curriculum is designed to encourage students to make connections between different areas of knowledge while developing their ability to analyse information, question ideas and approach challenges from different perspectives
How Do We Develop Independent and Global Learners?
The IB Diploma is designed to develop students as independent, reflective and open-minded learners. At ICS London, students are encouraged to take an active role in their education, ask thoughtful questions and engage with ideas beyond the classroom. They are supported to develop their own interests, challenge assumptions and make meaningful connections between their learning and the wider world.
This approach helps students develop the confidence to communicate their ideas, collaborate with others and consider different perspectives. Through both academic study and wider opportunities, students are encouraged to become curious, responsible and resilient learners. These qualities are an important part of preparing students for life in an increasingly international and interconnected world.
Learning Beyond the Classroom
The IB Diploma Programme at ICS London encourages students to become independent, curious and open-minded learners. Alongside developing strong academic knowledge, students are encouraged to think critically, make connections across subjects and engage with the wider world.
Through the core elements of the Diploma Programme, including Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS), students develop the skills, confidence and sense of responsibility to make a positive contribution beyond the classroom.
Globeducate Events
Students also have opportunities to take part in Globeducate events, connecting with peers from schools around the world through experiences such as the Globeducate Leadership Summit in the autumn term and Model United Nations (MUN) in the spring.
These experiences allow students to broaden their perspectives, develop their leadership and communication skills, and engage with global issues in an international community.
IGCSE to IBDP Progression
Our iGCSE programme provides a strong foundation for students progressing to the IBDP. Through a broad and academically challenging curriculum, students develop the subject knowledge, independent learning habits and critical-thinking skills that support success in the Diploma Programme.
The transition from iGCSE to IBDP is therefore a natural progression, with students building on the skills and knowledge they have developed while becoming increasingly independent and reflective learners.
Find out more about our iGCSE programme here.

iGCSE Programme
The iGCSE Programme in Years 10 and 11
At ICS London we offer students the opportunity to experience the best possible preparation for the IB Diploma Programme. Many of the topics studied at IGCSE level are also studied during IB Diploma, meaning that our IGCSE courses will build a strong foundation which will help students perform better in the IBDP.
IGCSEs are recognised worldwide by other schools and universities, and they can be used as proof of academic achievement, which is useful during the admissions process when applying to university. Some universities in the USA accept IGCSEs as a qualification similar to the US High School Diploma. This is because the US has a 4-year degree programme, and what would be covered in the IB Diploma is covered in the first year of study course in their universities.
IGCSES are a flexible curriculum and are adapted each year to meet the needs and interests of our students. The units are conceptual and inquiry-focused; therefore, topics, content, and texts may change. What follows is a sample curriculum.

pageCache.text:
AN IB SCHOOL IN LONDON
The International Baccalaureate at ICS London
Why choose the IB at ICS London?
The International Baccalaureate (IB) was founded on the belief that “Education for a better world” can empower young people to make a meaningful difference.
This vision closely aligns with the educational philosophy of ICS and Globeducate, where we inspire every student to become a confident, compassionate global citizen ready to shape the world around them.
Mission
As a non-profit educational foundation, the IB is driven by a clear mission: to create a better world through education.
Its commitment to developing curious, open-minded and globally minded learners makes it a natural fit with our own ambition to prepare students not only for academic success, but also to make a positive impact in the world.
A holistic education designed for all students
Comprised of three age-targeted stages, this international curriculum takes a holistic approach to education, fostering intellectual, personal, emotional, and social skills.
Our group-wide approach to teaching and learning will grow learners who are true pioneers and change-makers and our wider curricula will be constructed around the individual differences, specific talents, cultivating healthy competitiveness towards ourselves and giving each student the opportunity to access their first-choice university.
How to join the programme at ICS London
Interested in joining the IB programme at ICS London? Our admissions team can guide you through the application process, entry requirements and next steps for joining our international learning community.
Find out more about the IB programme and how to apply on our How to Apply page.
Career opportunities after the International Baccalaureate
The International Baccalaureate (IB) opens doors to a wide range of university and career opportunities around the world.
To learn more about the university pathways and opportunities available to ICS London students after the IB, visit our University & Careers page.
Extra-curricular activities
Beyond the classroom, students at ICS London have opportunities to take part in a wide range of extracurricular activities that complement their IB education.
From sports and creative arts to clubs, community projects and student-led initiatives, these activities encourage students to explore their interests, develop new skills and build confidence.
These activities also provide valuable opportunities to collaborate with others, take on leadership roles and strengthen the communication, creativity and teamwork skills that are central to the IB experience.
Find out more about our after-school offer here.
The PYP lays the foundations for lifelong learning by encouraging curiosity, creativity and independent thinking. Through inquiry-based learning, students explore meaningful questions, make connections across subjects and develop the academic, social and emotional skills they need to thrive. This approach nurtures open-minded, confident learners who are eager to discover the world around them. Read more here.
At ICS London, students follow the IB Middle Years Programme from ages 11 to 14. The MYP encourages students to make connections between their learning and the world around them through a broad, balanced and challenging curriculum. With an emphasis on inquiry, critical thinking and real-world applications, students develop the independence, creativity and problem-solving skills needed to become engaged, internationally minded learners. Read more here.
In Years 10 and 11, students study for their iGCSE qualifications within the wider IB educational framework. This pathway combines the academic rigour of iGCSEs with the IB’s emphasis on inquiry, critical thinking, international-mindedness and the development of the whole student. By bringing these approaches together, we prepare students for the next stage of their education, equipping them with the knowledge, skills and confidence to progress to the IB Diploma Programme or other post-16 pathways. Read more here.
The IB Diploma Programme is a challenging, internationally recognised pre-university qualification that prepares students for higher education and beyond. Students study a broad range of subjects while developing research, analytical and time-management skills. Alongside their academic studies, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS) encourage students to think critically, explore different perspectives and apply their learning to real-world contexts. The programme prepares students for university and helps them become thoughtful, engaged global citizens. Read more here.
The International Baccalaureate (IB) is a globally recognised educational framework that develops knowledgeable, curious and internationally minded students.
The IB places a strong emphasis on inquiry, critical thinking, independent learning and understanding different perspectives, preparing students for success at university and beyond.
At ICS London, students benefit from the IB educational approach throughout their school journey. Students follow the Primary Years Programme (PYP) and Middle Years Programme (MYP), with the MYP offered from ages 11 to 14. In Years 10 and 11, students study iGCSEs within the IB educational framework before progressing to the IB Diploma Programme (DP).
The IB approach is integrated throughout the school, beginning with the Early Years Programme (age 3) and continuing through the PYP, MYP, iGCSEs and IB Diploma Programme.
The specific programme a student joins depends on their age, educational background and year group when they enter ICS London.
Consult our year group placement guide here.
The IB goes beyond academic achievement. Students are encouraged to ask questions, think critically, make connections between subjects and apply their learning to the world around them. This holistic approach helps develop confident, independent and globally minded learners.
Students in Years 10 and 11 study iGCSEs, taught within the IB educational framework. This combines the academic rigour of internationally recognised iGCSE qualifications with the IB's focus on inquiry, critical thinking, independent learning and global perspectives.
Read more about the iGCSE programme here.
The IB develops skills that are valuable for higher education, including research, critical thinking, organisation, communication and independent learning. Its international recognition also supports students applying to universities in the UK and around the world.
Read more about university admission here.
Families interested in joining ICS London can find out more about our admissions process, entry requirements and how to apply through our Admissions page.
